questions.q: What dbatools cmdlet performs a SQL Server backup?
options: Save-DbaDatabase
New-DbaBackup
Export-DbaDatabase
Backup-DbaDatabase
questions.explain: Backup-DbaDatabase follows the Verb-DbaNoun convention and performs the same operation as T-SQL's BACKUP DATABASE statement.

questions.q: What values does the -Type parameter of Backup-DbaDatabase accept?
options: Sync and Async
Only Full
Small, Medium, Large
Full, Differential, or Log — the same three backup types taught in the SQL Server DBA course
questions.explain: These are the identical backup types from T-SQL BACKUP DATABASE, just invoked through a dbatools cmdlet instead.

questions.q: What happens if you call Backup-DbaDatabase against an instance without specifying -Database?
options: It throws an error and refuses to run
It only backs up the master database
It backs up every user database on the instance, avoiding the need to write an explicit loop
It backs up a randomly chosen database
questions.explain: Omitting -Database backs up all user databases on the instance — a convenience that would otherwise require hand-written looping logic.

questions.q: In the lesson's script example, what determines whether a full or differential backup runs on a given day?
options: It cannot be automated and must be chosen manually each time
The size of the database
An if/else branch checking (Get-Date).DayOfWeek, replacing what would otherwise be three separately maintained SQL Server Agent job schedules
A random number generator
questions.explain: PowerShell's real conditional logic lets one script express the same full/differential/log cadence that used to require separate Agent job schedules.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what actually changes between a T-SQL/Agent-based backup strategy and a Backup-DbaDatabase-based one?
options: The RPO and RTO targets change completely
Retention policy concepts no longer apply
PowerShell backups are not real SQL Server backups
The execution engine — real conditionals, error handling, and multi-server scripting — while the underlying backup strategy (RPO/RTO, backup types, cadence) stays the same
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as the same strategy running on a more capable execution engine, not a new backup strategy.
